newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel oil trades above low sulphur.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel oil trades above low sulphur.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel oil prices were firmer yet again on Friday and an ARA cargo traded at higher levels than a low sulphur cargo deal sourced from the same region, traders said.
A trader seeking to fill committments into Portugal bought a cargo out of the barge market at a hefty $109 fob ARA.
A large Italian end user bought a 30,000 tonne low sulphur cargo loading in Antwerp next week at $106 fob ARA.
Traders were surprised by both deals, as September high sulphur cargo swaps traded at $110-$111.25 cif NWE and September low sulphur cargo swaps were heard bid at $111.75 fob NWE.
Dealers said the Antwerp cargo quality meant it was probably worth around $2 a tonne less than a full ENEL type cargo.
The trader was seen needing between one and three more for the Portuguese tender but now holds at least five cargoes.
Other potential utility buyers backed away from the market. "I am trying desperately to keep out of this mess," one said.
A Scandinavian player was heard holding, but not actively offering, a late-month cargo. One dealer said he had heard the seller would consider bids at around $115 cif NWE.
